summary: Behaviorist Matthew Israel founded the Behavior Research Institute in 1971, later the Judge Rotenberg Center in Massachusetts, where disabled and autistic students were pinched, restrained and given electric shocks for decades.

evidence.note: Israel born in Brookline sometime in the 1930s; host found no exact year
Skinner and behaviorism get a long segment as Israel's formative influence
Behavior Research Institute founded in Providence, Rhode Island in 1971
California branch shut down for unlicensed practice; later runs as a parent co-op
Massachusetts probate judge Rotenberg rules aversives may continue; school renamed for him
Israel builds the GED shock device after the SIBIS makers refuse to raise its strength
2007 prank call leads to two teens shocked dozens of times; 2011 indictment and exit
FDA ban on shock devices overturned by an appeals court in 2021; school still operating

notes: Israel's birth year is not given (host says the 1930s), so lifespan start is null and covered_span starts at an estimated 1930. His death status is not addressed; end left null. Massachusetts is the main state, but Rhode Island and California also have real segments. Some victims were adults (e.g. a 25-year-old student), but most were minors.
